A recorded example of the response OpenRouter returns after a primary model's transport failure (rate limit) triggers its own provider-array fallback (extra.models on the seat) and a fallback model successfully answers instead. The outbound request this responds to is what test/openrouter-adapter-capabilities.test.js's 'provider-array variant 1' test already proves the adapter sends verbatim - this fixture is the other side, the response. OpenRouter's own response `model` field names whichever model actually answered, which may differ from the request's primary `model` - that's the whole point of fallback, and is why chain.js/report.json must read the RESPONSE's model, never assume the request's primary model answered. No live OpenRouter URL was fetched to produce this fixture.
